record.original_question: Fix an integer k >= 1 and let n = 4k + 1. Choose a set S subseteq {1, 2, ..., 2k} of size k, let the complementary set {1, ..., 2k} \ S be used on the second layer, and define the extended Petersen graph XP(2n, S) on vertex set Z_n x {1, 2} with layer edges determined by circular distance d(x, y) = min{|x - y|, n - |x - y|} and matching edges x1x2 for x in Z_n. Is every extended Petersen graph, except the Petersen graph itself, Class 1, meaning that its chromatic index equals its maximum degree?

evidence.quote: Let n = 4k + 1 for some integer k >= 1, and let S subseteq {1, 2, . . . , 2k} such that |S| = k. The extended Petersen graph XP(2n, S) is a graph with the vertex set V = Z_n x {1, 2}, and the edge set E = {x1y1 : d(x1, y1) in S} union {x2y2 : d(x2, y2) in S-bar} union {x1x2 : x in Z_n}, where S-bar = {1, . . . , 2k} \ S and d(x, y) = min{|x - y|, n - |x - y|}.
Conjecture 3.1 (Horak, Rosa [1]) Every extended Petersen graph, except Petersen graph itself, is of Class 1.
A graph G is Class 1 if it is Delta(G)-edge-colorable, otherwise it is Class 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $k\geq 1$ and set $n=4k+1$. For $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ define the circular distance $d(x,y)=\min\{|x-y|,\,n-|x-y|\}$. Choose any subset $S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,2k\}$ with $|S|=k$, and let $\bar S=\{1,2,\ldots,2k\}\setminus S$. The extended Petersen graph $XP(2n,S)$ has vertex set $V=\mathbb{Z}_n\times\{1,2\}$ and edge set
$$E=\{x_1y_1:d(x,y)\in S\}\cup\{x_2y_2:d(x,y)\in\bar S\}\cup\{x_1x_2:x\in\mathbb{Z}_n\},$$
where $x_i$ denotes $(x,i)$. Recall that the chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ is the minimum number of colors needed for a proper edge-coloring, and by Vizing's theorem $\chi'(G)\in\{\Delta(G),\Delta(G)+1\}$; $G$ is said to be of Class 1 if $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)$ and Class 2 otherwise.

Prove or disprove: for every $k\geq 1$ and every admissible choice of $S$, the graph $XP(2n,S)$ is of Class 1, with the sole exception of the Petersen graph itself (the case $k=1$, $n=5$, $S=\{2\}$).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to Horák and Rosa, is presented as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems from a graph theory workshop. No published resolution was located via web search; results on chromatic indices of related generalized Petersen graphs exist, but the specific conjecture for extended Petersen graphs $XP(2n,S)$ appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems compilation (arXiv 2411.10046)
status_evidence.snippet: The paper collects open problems presented by participants of a graph theory workshop, including the conjecture that every extended Petersen graph except the Petersen graph itself is Class 1.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed as an open problem in this 2024 compilation.

status_evidence.title: Petersen graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Petersen graph has chromatic index 4 (it is a snark), so it is Class 2.
status_evidence.claim: The Petersen graph itself is the known Class 2 exception.
